chunks: 5508 - And it was narrated from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Naṣr al-Bazanṭī, who said:

I copied from a book in the handwriting of Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام: A certain person, your mawla, passed away. A son of his brother died, and he left behind an umm walad belonging to him who had no child. He bequeathed to her one thousand dirhams. Is the bequest valid, and does emancipation take effect upon her? What is her status? Your opinion in that matter—may my soul be your ransom.
So he عليه السلام wrote: She is freed from the one-third, and the bequest belongs to her.

key_terms.أَلْفِ دِرْهَمٍ: one thousand dirhams, the amount specified in the bequest
key_terms.أُمَّ وَلَدٍ: an umm walad, a slave-concubine linked to her master through childbirth status
key_terms.الثُّلُثِ: one-third of the estate, the portion from which certain bequests are executed
key_terms.الْوَصِيَّةُ: the bequest or testamentary gift made by the deceased
key_terms.تُعْتَقُ: she is to be freed or emancipated

ai.seo_question: Is a bequest to an umm walad valid, and can her emancipation be taken from one-third of the estate?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning an umm walad for whom a deceased man made a bequest. The Imam عليه السلام rules that her emancipation is effected from one-third of the estate and that the bequest made to her is valid. It is significant in the jurisprudence of wills, estate distribution, and the legal status of dependent women.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5508 - It was narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr Al-Bazanti, who said:

I copied from a book in the handwriting of Abu Al-Hasan (as):
"A certain person, your master, passed away, leaving behind a paternal nephew who also passed away. The nephew left behind an umm walad (a concubine who bore him no children) and bequeathed to her a thousand dirhams. Does the bequest hold validity, and does she receive emancipation? What is her status? May I be your ransom, I seek your opinion on this matter."
Imam (as) wrote back: "She is to be freed from one-third (of the estate), and she has the bequest."
